name: Aesthetic Taste
subtitle: Aesthetic Sensitivity
instructions: Rate each statement from 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 5 (Strongly Agree), based on your genuine reactions, not what sounds sophisticated or culturally appropriate.

questions.text: When you hear something loud and energetic in music, with distorted guitars or aggressive drumming, it draws you in rather than putting you off.
There is something in the rawness and intensity of harder music that you find genuinely appealing, a sense of energy that softer music doesn't give you.
You find yourself attracted to music that has a rebellious or defiant quality to it, something that feels like it's pushing against something.
The boldness and directness of harder, louder music speaks to something in you that more polished or gentle music often misses.
When a piece of music is abrasive or uncomfortable on purpose, you find that more interesting than something that goes out of its way to be pleasant.
You are drawn to art or music that has an edge to it, something with tension or darkness that makes it feel more alive.
The kind of music that feels almost physically intense, where you can feel the energy in your chest, appeals to you.
You find that work which is deliberately unconventional or provocative tends to interest you more than work that stays within familiar boundaries.
When a song has a hook that stays with you all day, something simple and immediately catchy, you find that genuinely satisfying rather than cheap.
Music that is produced to sound polished and radio-ready has a kind of pleasure in it that you don't feel the need to apologize for.
You find that upbeat, danceable music puts you in a better mood in a way that more serious or complex music often doesn't.
There is something enjoyable about music that is openly emotional and sentimental, even when it doesn't try to be subtle about it.
You find yourself drawn to music that is designed to be enjoyed widely, something people can share and sing along to.
When a song is melodically strong and immediately satisfying, you value that quality even if it isn't particularly complex.
You have genuine affection for music that is fun and light in a deliberate way, without needing it to be deep.
You find that music which is warm, familiar in its structure, and designed to feel good does exactly that for you.
Music that feels rooted in something older, folk traditions, acoustic instruments, a sense of place or history, appeals to you in a way that more modern styles don't always reach.
You find music that tells a story or has a strong connection to a particular culture or tradition more interesting than music that avoids those roots.
There is something in music that sounds like it grew out of a specific community or landscape, rather than being made in a studio, that you find genuinely moving.
Acoustic, stripped-back music, where you can hear the room or the breath of the performer, tends to feel more real to you than heavily produced music.
You are drawn to music that has an improvisational or spontaneous quality, where it sounds like the musicians are responding to each other in real time.
Music that reflects real life experiences, loss, work, place, time passing, connects with you more than music that keeps things abstract or aspirational.
You find something appealing about musical forms that have been passed down and refined over generations, rather than invented recently.
The sound of traditional instruments played in their natural context, a fiddle in a folk setting, a banjo on a porch, has an authenticity that appeals to you.
Standing in front of a painting or photograph that is genuinely well made produces something more than intellectual appreciation in you, it actually moves you.
You notice visual quality in everyday things, the way light falls, the proportions of an object, the color of a surface, in places where most people see nothing remarkable.
You have strong preferences about visual things. Certain colors, compositions, and styles feel right to you in a way that others clearly don't.
The visual quality of your surroundings has a real effect on your mood. An ugly space or a beautiful one makes a genuine difference to how you feel in it.
You notice visual details that most people pass over entirely, texture, the quality of light, how a space is balanced.
You can lose yourself in looking at something visually striking. Time disappears when you are standing in front of a painting or looking out at a landscape.
